title: Reading a balance sheet in ten minutes
excerpt: A practical walk through assets, liabilities and what they say about risk.
author: Nishant Jain
articleHtml:
Start with the equation: assets equal liabilities plus equity. Everything else is detail.

Then ask three questions: how much is borrowed, how quickly can short-term bills be paid, and is equity growing from profit or from fresh share issues?

Finally, compare two years side by side. Trends tell you more than any single number.

title: Why cash conversion matters more than profit
excerpt: Profit is an opinion; cash is a fact. How to check one against the other.
author: Nishant Jain
articleHtml:
Divide operating cash flow by net profit. Around 100% or more means profit is turning into cash.

A company can report rising profit for years while cash stays flat: receivables and inventory are quietly absorbing it.

Check the ratio over five years, not one.

title: Margin of safety in Indian mid-caps
excerpt: How we size positions when the range of outcomes is wide.
author: Nishant Jain
articleHtml:
A margin of safety is the gap between what you pay and a conservative estimate of what a business is worth.

In mid-caps the range of outcomes is wide, so positions stay small until the evidence is strong.
